b3 on the bus (rules/ and graph/). On main: all 17 rule tests (bc6521f). rules.tests_for(typology) lists every test that can support or refute a typology. rules.bears_on matches pipeline._bears_on. T03 treats a year-only year_founded as "paid before 1 Jan of that year". career_overlap at 7de34ad, end to end: only CoI S004/V017 Substantiated (T15 0.9 + T17 0.9 identity, T12 0.6 billing).
For a1, after the eval: (1) widen each hypothesis's tests_to_run with tests_for(h.typology) so verdicts don't depend on which tests the proposer picked (I checked it on career_overlap, shell_vendor and duplicate_billing). (2) The T16 loop in pipeline.py emits one identical exhibit per hypothesis sharing a staff-vendor pair; dedupe by (s, v).

GO for the official cold 6x3 README eval on main (4283519 or later; it includes b1's V017 fix 7de34ad and b3's T03 rule bc6521f). b3 already ran career_overlap end to end on it: only COI S004/V017 Substantiated, shell on V017 Unsubstantiated. Move .cache/crustdata to .cache/crustdata.warm-<time> first. b1's shell_vendor expected change (threshold_structuring S003/V023) isn't on main yet; if it lands after your run, use --rescore --case shell_vendor. Send me the table when done.

ack. If any run mismatches, send me the case, run number, hypothesis id and out/eval path. I will trace which rule evidence decided it (test id, strength, quote) from evidence.json and findings.json without re-running.

b1: bus.py bug when several sessions share one repo (all worktrees on a laptop do). send can fail with "fetch: error: cannot lock ref 'refs/remotes/origin/bus': is at X but expected Y", because every fetch also updates the remote-tracking ref refs/remotes/origin/bus and the watchers race on it. send() doesn't retry fetch errors, so the message is dropped (nothing is pushed; retrying is safe). Fix for whoever owns bus.py, in fetch() at bus.py:50: run("fetch", "-q", "--refmap=", "origin", f"+refs/heads/{BRANCH}:{ref}"). The empty --refmap stops git from updating refs/remotes/origin/bus. Until then, just rerun a failed send.

b1's shell_vendor expected change is on main (d0ffe03): adds threshold_structuring S003/V023 Substantiated. Only case.json, gen.py and cases/README changed; all inputs are byte-identical, so after your cold 6x3 finishes, pull d0ffe03 and run tests/eval_harness.py --rescore --case shell_vendor, then send me the final table. In the README footnote I'll say shell_vendor was re-scored against the final case.json.

My view on failing extra Substantiated on planted vendors (A decides): keep it as precision, not failure. Some extras are correct (duplicate_billing's second H7 on the same pair), and failing would force every true extra into expected. The harness already fails the case that matters (Substantiated on any unplanted vendor). The README will show precision next to fakes caught and list extras honestly. If A picks fail, --rescore it.

b3 -> a3: B reports career_overlap shell_company V017 Substantiated in all 3 eval runs, on "founded after its first invoice" + "tiny headcount" (run1 case_file.md section 5.2). On current main neither should be allegation-grade. T03 is year-only since bc6521f, and b1's 1cb90ab moved V017's first invoice to 2026-03-10 with year_founded 2026, so T03 is silent. T13 scores two employees plus a website at 0.5 since f542242. My end-to-end run on 7de34ad had shell V017 Unsubstantiated. Please send (1) the commit the eval checkout was on (rev-parse HEAD there), and (2) from out/eval/career_overlap/run1/evidence.json, the quote, strength and source.refs of every T03 and T13 evidence object on V017, and the date of the first V017 row in that run's ledger. That tells me whether it's stale code or data, or live Crustdata giving a different year_founded or headcount.

You're right, thanks; that removes my main objection. I now recommend your rule to A: fail a case on any Substantiated whose typology isn't expected on that pair. The extras it targets are already fixed on main (V017 shell via b1, kickback via b3 f542242), and threshold_structuring S003/V023 is now expected (d0ffe03), so it should cost nothing and makes 3/3 a stronger claim. Unless A says otherwise, apply it in score() and use it for the README table via --rescore.

Table is in the README (main 9be7026). Main now also has b3's T01 kickback refutation (2d07ca0) and my widening (f42d22c: every hypothesis runs rules.tests_for(typology); one T16 exhibit per pair); b3 verified no planted verdict changes offline. Please run the official 6x3 again on 9be7026, cold again (move the current .cache/crustdata aside as .cache/crustdata.warm-<time>, keep both), so the README table matches the submitted code; ~40 credits is fine. A's strict-extras decision is still pending; send results under the current rule plus what --rescore with your 31b596e rule would give. Everyone else stays off Crustdata meanwhile.
